## Scope of this Part and interpretation

## 58.1

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (1) This Part applies to claims in the Commercial Court of the King’s Bench Division.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (2) In this Part and Practice Direction 58, ‘commercial claim’ means any claim arising out of the transaction of trade and commerce and includes any claim relating to –

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (a) a business document or contract;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (b) the export or import of goods;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (c) the carriage of goods by land, sea, air or pipeline;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (d) the exploitation of oil and gas reserves or other natural resources;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (e) insurance and re-insurance;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (f) banking and financial services;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (g) the operation of markets and exchanges;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (h) the purchase and sale of commodities;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (i) the construction of ships;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (j) business agency; and

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.1] (k) arbitration.

## Specialist list

## 58.2

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.2] (1) The commercial list is a specialist list for claims proceeding in the Commercial Court.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.2] (2) One of the judges of the Commercial Court shall be in charge of the commercial list.

## Application of the Civil Procedure Rules

## 58.3

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.3] These Rules and their practice directions apply to claims in the commercial list unless this Part or a practice direction provides otherwise.

## Proceedings in the commercial list

## 58.4

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.4] (1) A commercial claim may be started in the commercial list.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.4] (2) Rule 30.5 applies to claims in the commercial list, except that a Commercial Court judge may order a claim to be transferred to any other specialist list.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.4] (Rule 30.5(3) provides that an application for the transfer of proceedings to or from a specialist list must be made to a judge dealing with claims in that list.)

## Claim form and particulars of claim

## 58.5

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (1) If, in a Part 7 claim, particulars of claim are not contained in or served with the claim form –

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (a) the claim form must state that, if an acknowledgment of service is filed which indicates an intention to defend the claim, particulars of claim will follow;

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (b) when the claim form is served, it must be accompanied by the documents specified in rule 7.8(1);

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (c) the claimant must serve particulars of claim within 28 days of the filing of an acknowledgment of service which indicates an intention to defend; and

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (d) rule 7.4(2) does not apply.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (2) A statement of value is not required to be included in the claim form.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (3) If the claimant is claiming interest, he must –

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (a) include a statement to that effect; and

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] (b) give the details set out in rule 16.4(2),

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.5] in both the claim form and the particulars of claim.

## Acknowledgment of service

## 58.6

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.6] (1) A defendant must file an acknowledgment of service in every case.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.6] (2) Unless paragraph (3) applies, the period for filing an acknowledgment of service is 14 days after service of the claim form.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.6] (3) Where the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction, or on the agent of a defendant who is overseas, the time periods provided by rules 6.12(3), 6.35 and 6.37(5) apply after service of the claim form.

## Disputing the court’s jurisdiction

## 58.7

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.7] (1) Part 11 applies to claims in the commercial list with the modifications set out in this rule.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.7] (2) An application under rule 11(1) must be made within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.7] (3) If the defendant files an acknowledgment of service indicating an intention to dispute the court’s jurisdiction, the claimant need not serve particulars of claim before the hearing of the application.

## Default judgment

## 58.8

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.8] (1) If, in a Part 7 claim in the commercial list, a defendant fails to file an acknowledgment of service, the claimant need not serve particulars of claim before he may obtain or apply for default judgment in accordance with Part 12.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.8] (2) Rule 12.7(1) applies with the modification that paragraph (a) shall be read as if it referred to the claim form instead of the particulars of claim.

## Admissions

## 58.9

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.9] (1) Where the claim is for a specified amount of money and the defendant admits part of the claim, the claimant may apply under Part 14 for judgment on the admission but rules 14.2 and 14.6(5) to (7) do not apply.

## Defence and Reply

## 58.10

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.10] (1) Part 15 (defence and reply) applies to claims in the commercial list with the modification to rule 15.8(a) that the claimant must –

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.10] (a) file any reply to a defence; and

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.10] (b) serve it on all other parties,

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.10] within 21 days after service of the defence.

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.10] (2) Rule 6.35 (in relation to the period for filing a defence where the claim form is served out of the jurisdiction) applies to claims in the commercial list, except that if the particulars of claim are served after the defendant has filed an acknowledgment of service the period for filing a defence is 28 days from service of the particulars of claim.

## Statements of case

## 58.11

[PART 58 – COMMERCIAL COURT > 58.11] The court may at any time before or after the issue of the claim form order a claim in the commercial list to proceed without the filing or service of statements of case.

## Part 8 claims

## 58.12

# Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service.

## Case management

## 58.13

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (1) All proceedings in the commercial list are treated as being allocated to the multi-track and Part 26 does not apply.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (2) The following parts only of Part 29 apply –

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (a) rule 29.3(2) (legal representative to attend case management conferences and pre-trial reviews);

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (b) rule 29.5 (variation of case management timetable) with the exception of rule 29.5(1)(c); and

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (c) rule 29.2(1A) (order or encourage to engage in alternative dispute resolution).

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (3) As soon as practicable the court will hold a case management conference which must be fixed in accordance with Practice Direction 58.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.13] (4) At the case management conference or at any hearing at which the parties are represented the court may give such directions for the management of the case as it considers appropriate.

## Disclosure – ships papers

## 58.14

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.14] (1) If, in proceedings relating to a marine insurance policy, the underwriters apply for specific disclosure under rule 31.12, the court may –

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.14] (a) order a party to produce all the ships papers; and

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.14] (b) require that party to use his best endeavours to obtain and disclose documents which are not or have not been in his control.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.14] (2) An order under this rule may be made at any stage of the proceedings and on such terms, if any, as to staying the proceedings or otherwise, as the court thinks fit.

## Judgments and orders

## 58.15

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.15] (1) Except for orders made by the court on its own initiative and unless the court orders otherwise, every judgment or order will be drawn up by the parties, and rule 40.3 is modified accordingly.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.15] (2) An application for a consent order must include a draft of the proposed order signed on behalf of all the parties to whom it relates.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.15] (3) Rule 40.6 (consent judgments and orders) does not apply.

[Part 8 applies to claims in the commercial list, with the modification that a defendant to a Part 8 claim who wishes to rely on written evidence must file and serve it within 28 days after filing an acknowledgment of service. > 58.15] Updated: Sunday, 1 October 2023
